---
title: "Enhanced Consumer Participation Model (ECPM)"
subtitle: "A 1990 training project later described as a step toward CSIL"
---

::: {.callout-note}
## What this page covers
The Enhanced Consumer Participation Model (ECPM) is the name of a training project from around 1990. A later bibliography confirms that a skill-development manual existed, but we have not found a copy to read.

This page uses that bibliography for the 1990 manual, later organizational and training accounts for the project name, and a 1994 Van der Klift publication that is **not** an ECPM manual. It does **not** treat ECPM as a proven official predecessor of CSIL. A distinct 1994 ECPM training manual remains an open identity question.
:::

## How to read this page

Statements below are labelled in ordinary language:

- **Listed in a bibliography** — a finding aid we have read confirms title, creators, date, or physical description; this archive has not seen the work itself
- **Documented from a later source** — taken from a later page or slide deck that was read
- **Later recollection** — a later named account; this archive is not independently asserting it
- **Interpretation** — inferred from those sources, and said to be so
- **Open question** — not settled by the sources we have read

When accounts from the time, or bibliographic listings, differ from later accounts, the earlier evidence is preferred. Later IFRC and Gauthier wording is not treated as a 1990s ministry regulation or contract.

## What ECPM can be documented as

The strongest independently verifiable public description is a bibliography entry, not a recovered manual.

The [Roeher Institute / Brian Salisbury annotated bibliography](../sources/1990s-roeher-if-bibliography.qmd) (a late-1990s finding aid we have read as a PDF) lists:

> BC Rehab & Greater Vancouver Home Support Society  
> “Enhanced Consumer Participation Model: Skill Development Manual for Consumers of Home Support Services”, BC Rehab & Greater Vancouver Home Support Society, 1990  
> A training manual that includes 5 modules intended to empower consumers to act as effective employers (52 pages plus appendices)

**Listed in a bibliography:** a 1990 skill-development manual existed under the ECPM name; it was issued by BC Rehab and Greater Vancouver Home Support Society; it had five modules and was described as training consumers to act as employers.

**What that citation does not show.** The bibliography does not name personal authors, a place of publication, an ISBN, a revision history, or a relationship to CSIL. This archive has not read the manual and must not paraphrase module contents we have not seen.

Later sources use “ECPM” as a **named project**, not only as a manual title:

- [IFRC “Our Team”](../sources/ifrc-our-team.qmd) (a later organizational page we have read) calls ECPM “the individual funding project” that preceded CSIL.
- [Gauthier 2014](../sources/2014-gauthier-sci-csil-presentation.qmd) (a later training deck we have read) lists “ECPM Enhanced Consumer Participation Model” under “Pre CSIL?” with “The Agency” and “People paid themselves.”

Those are **later reconstructions**. They support treating ECPM as a name later writers attach to a pre-CSIL individualized-funding arrangement. They do not supply a program regulation, contract, or ministry document from the 1990s.

Current [Vancouver Coastal Health CSIL service pages](../sources/vch-csil-service-page.qmd) do **not** use the ECPM name. Survival of the acronym at Vancouver Coastal Health is not documented.

## Organizations and people supported by evidence

| Person or body | What the sources we have read support | What they do not support |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BC Rehab / BC Rehabilitation Society | Corporate author of the 1990 manual in Roeher | Personal editors; legal continuity into later health authorities |
| Greater Vancouver Home Support Society | Co-author of the 1990 manual in Roeher | A recovered society file; later Vancouver Coastal Health succession as an ECPM office |
| [Joseph Theriault](../people/joseph-theriault.qmd) | IFRC later wording: worked with Paul Gauthier and others on the individual-funding project “then known as” ECPM | Any name on the unread 1990 title page; a job title from the time |
| [Paul Gauthier](../people/paul-gauthier.qmd) | Later IFRC/Gauthier materials place him in a pre-CSIL / CSIL founding story that *names* ECPM | An ECPM appointment from the time; authorship of the 1990 manual |
| [Emma Van der Klift](../people/emma-van-der-klift.qmd) | Author, with Norman Kunc, of a **different** 1994 chapter ([*Hell-Bent on Helping*](../sources/1994-van-der-klift-hell-bent.qmd)) | Authorship of a 1994 ECPM training manual; any ECPM credit we have seen |
| Vancouver Health Department | Named only in early project notes as a possible 1994-manual affiliate | Any 1990s document we have read using that affiliation for ECPM |

: Documented and excluded ECPM roles, from sources this archive has read

No source we have read names a design committee or proves that any of these people sat on a later CSIL design group **because of** ECPM. Design-group membership is not inferred here.

Search-engine restatements of the Roeher entry are **not** counted as independent confirmation. A later bibliography confirms that the manual existed, but we have not found a copy to read.

## The unresolved 1994-manual question

A possible 1994 ECPM training revision appears in early project notes. It is **not** listed in the Roeher bibliography we have read. No public full text, catalogue holding, or second independent citation was recovered.

[Van der Klift and Kunc, “Hell-Bent on Helping” (1994)](../sources/1994-van-der-klift-hell-bent.qmd) is a published chapter on help and inclusive education. The Broadreach republication we have read does **not** name ECPM, CSIL, BC Rehab, Greater Vancouver Home Support Society, or Vancouver Health Department. It is a **near-miss**: a real 1994 Van der Klift publication from the same year as the hypothesized manual, not bibliographic evidence that she wrote or revised an ECPM text.

We do not have enough evidence to decide whether the reported 1994 item is a distinct work, a revision of the 1990 manual, a conflicting citation of the same 1990 work, or a confusion with *Hell-Bent on Helping*.

This is not yet a contradiction between two bibliographic records we have read. It is one 1990 citation we have read versus later uncited project notes.

## Relationship to later CSIL

| Claim | Status | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Later IFRC wording treats ECPM as the individual-funding project that preceded CSIL | Later recollection | [IFRC Our Team](../sources/ifrc-our-team.qmd) |
| Later Gauthier slides list ECPM as a “Pre CSIL?” step | Later recollection | [Gauthier 2014](../sources/2014-gauthier-sci-csil-presentation.qmd) |
| Creekview became ECPM, or ECPM became CSIL, by a formal document | Open question | No 1990s document we have read says so. The [Creekview chapter](creekview.qmd) does not establish that link. |
| Current Vancouver Coastal Health pages continue the ECPM name | Not supported | [VCH CSIL page](../sources/vch-csil-service-page.qmd) |

: What later sources say about ECPM and CSIL — not a proven succession

**Interpretation, and no further:** ECPM is a named 1990 training and manual project (from a bibliography) and a named pre-CSIL individualized-funding idea in later participant and organizational accounts. Those two uses may describe the same effort, related efforts, or a later label applied to earlier work. This archive does **not** convert that overlap into a proven official succession.

[*Keys on Freedom*](../sources/wanted-keys-on-freedom.qmd) remains unconfirmed (title, author, and year still come only from early project notes). Roeher does not list it. No relationship to the 1990 ECPM manual is established.

## What we still do not know

1. Full text, title-page authors, place, ISBN, and module titles of the 1990 manual.
2. Whether a 1994 ECPM training manual exists as a distinct document.
3. Whether Van der Klift, Theriault, Gauthier, Greater Vancouver Home Support Society staff, or Vancouver Health Department appear on any ECPM title page.
4. What program, contract, or agency arrangement from the time “ECPM” named besides the manual.
5. Whether *Keys on Freedom* is related, identical in purpose, or unrelated.
6. Whether any 1990s Ministry of Health file uses the ECPM name in connection with CSIL design.

Leads are listed on the [wanted ECPM manuals record](../sources/wanted-ecpm-manuals.qmd).
